The Authentic Name

Why enlīl.com is the correct form

Mesopotamian Original

Enlīl

The name in its original Mesopotamian form. The original script is preserved in scholarly transliteration systems.

ASCII Constraint

ENLIL

Stripped of its identity, the name was reduced to plain Latin letters. The original orthography — stress, length, breathing — was erased by systems that only understand A-Z.

Unicode Restoration

Enlīl

The Unicode restoration recovers what ASCII destroyed. This is philological accuracy — not decoration. The domain encodes to Punycode, but the browser displays the truth.

Valid Scholarly Variations
Enlil enlīl Ellil

Each variant is an attested scholarly orthography. The owned form is the active domain; others are historically valid alternatives.

Punycode Encoding
enlīl.com → xn--enll-sya.com

The non-ASCII characters in Enlīl are encoded while the ASCII remains visible. To the DNS, it is Punycode. To humanity, it is Enlīl.

Mythology & Lore

The supreme Mesopotamian storm lord

Enlīl was the supreme god of the Sumerian pantheon and, through syncretism, the chief deity of Assyria and Babylonia. His name means “Lord Wind” or “Lord Air,” and his authority was cosmic: he decreed the fates, commanded storms, and held the Tablets of Destiny.

Enlīl dwelt in the Ekur (“Mountain House”), the temple complex in Nippur that was considered the religious center of Sumer. Unlike local city gods, his cult transcended individual city-states; kings from across Mesopotamia sought his blessing.

The myth Enlil and Ninlil tells how the young god was banished from Nippur for seducing the goddess Ninlil, followed her to the underworld, and there fathered three chthonic deities — including Nanna/Sin, the moon god. This story binds together heaven, earth, and the netherworld under Enlīl’s lineage.

After the rise of Babylon, Enlīl’s cosmic role was partly absorbed by Marduk, but his importance never fully faded. In Assyria he remained a national god, invoked in royal inscriptions and treaties.

07

Pronunciation

How to say the name

Standard: /ˈɛnlɪl/ (two short syllables, stress on the first).

With the macron preserved: /ɛnˈliːl/ or /ˈɛnliːl/, depending on whether one stresses the long second vowel. The owned form Enlīl makes the length visible; the plain spelling Enlil is what most reference works print.

09

Syncretism

Enlīl across Mesopotamia

Sumerian Enlil became Akkadian Ellil as Semitic-speaking rulers adopted the older Sumerian pantheon. The name and role remained largely unchanged, though pronunciation shifted.

Babylonian period: As Marduk rose to supremacy in Babylon, Enlīl’s cosmic functions were increasingly attributed to Marduk, yet Enlīl retained his ancient prestige and was still invoked as the great father of gods.

Assyrian period: The Assyrians continued to honor Enlīl (often under the name Ellil) as a royal patron. His temple at Assur remained one of the most important religious sites of the empire.

10

Cultural Legacy

The lord wind in the modern world

Enlīl is one of the best-known deities of the ancient Near East. His myths, especially the Epic of Gilgamesh and Enlil and Ninlil, remain standard reading in ancient history and religious studies.

His imagery — the storm-god who decrees destiny from a mountain temple — influenced later conceptions of high gods across the region. The name appears in academic literature, video games, fantasy novels, and modern pagan revival groups as a symbol of sovereign air and command.
